policy: No file in ~/Downloads/IP-SAKTI Corpus is ever replaced in place. Acquired copies land in data/source_updates/ under content-addressed names and supersede a local source only after an explicit approval step and a fresh ingestion run.

priority_key.2: replacement required (stale, wrong content, or unresolved provenance)

candidates_held_but_not_accepted.assessment: Contains the right text: Regulations 1 to 14 and Schedules A, B, C and D of the Food Safety and Standards (Ayurveda Aahara) Regulations, 2022, including the definition of Ayurveda Aahara, the Schedule A list of 71 authoritative books and the Schedule B category table. Rejected as a source of record on two grounds. First, provenance: the file is an mPDF/Laravel print-to-PDF stamped 'Printed For: 29-08-2026' and carrying the LegitQuest logo on every page — a commercial database, which §2 excludes. Second, completeness: it ends inside Schedule D, so Schedule E (the AYURVEDA AAHARA logo, which regulation 13(a) makes mandatory on every label) is referenced but never reproduced, and there is no gazette masthead or signature block. Useful as a cross-check while the official text is sought; not admissible as the citable source.

recommended_source.title: Food Safety and Standards (Ayurveda Aahara) Regulations, 2022
recommended_source.publisher: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

documents.reason: The most Ayurveda-specific instrument on the expected list, and the corpus does not contain it. What the corpus has instead is the FSSAI covering Order of 25 July 2025 (registered as IN-FSSAI-AYURVEDA-AAHARA-2022) whose filename claims to be these Regulations. Made under section 92(2)(v) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006; draft published 30 June 2021, gazette copies released to the public 5 July 2021, final notification dated 5 May 2022. The FSSAI gazette URL located in this phase serves the site's JavaScript shell rather than a PDF, and the FSSAI 'Ayurveda Aahara Compendium' turns out to be another recipe index. Acquisition probably needs a browser session against the FSSAI portal or a request to FSSAI directly.

recommended_source.title: The Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (Act No. 18 of 2003)

documents.reason: The amending Act the local copy claims to incorporate was confirmed directly from the Gazette: the Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023 is Act 10 of 2023, assented 3 August 2023 (egazette.gov.in). The consolidation looks right; only its publisher is unknown. nbaindia.org now redirects to nbaindia.nic.in and the old PDF paths are dead — re-acquire through the NBA site's own navigation.

recommended_source.title: The Copyright Act, 1957 (Act No. 14 of 1957)
recommended_source.publisher: Copyright Office, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, Ministry of Commerce and Industry

documents.reason: Both copies predate a passed amendment. The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2026, Serial 23 of its Schedule, omits section 67; section 67 ('Penalty for making false entries in register') is still present in full in the local copy AND in the Copyright Office copy. Commencement is by notification under section 1(2) and no commencement notification was located, so the amendment's in-force date is unconfirmed. Replace with the Copyright Office copy for provenance, and re-check once a post-commencement consolidation appears.

recommended_source.title: The Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 (Act 23 of 1940)
recommended_source.publisher: Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation, Directorate General of Health Services, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

documents.reason: STALE by nine years, and amended since: the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2026 amends section 27A of this Act (confirmed in the Gazette text at Serial 22 of its Schedule). CDSCO publishes the Act separately, released 22 November 2022.

recommended_source.title: The Drugs Rules, 1945
recommended_source.publisher: CDSCO, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

documents.reason: STALE by eight years, and the replacement has been acquired and its currency read from the document itself: the CDSCO consolidated Drugs Rules, 1945 runs to 963 pages and its front matter states '[As amended vide G.S.R. 360(E) dated 01-07-2024 (w.e.f. 01-07-2024)]'. That is 366 pages more than the local Rules. Note also that the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019 and the Cosmetics Rules, 2020 have since carved subject matter out of the 1945 Rules.

recommended_source.title: The Designs Rules, 2001
recommended_source.publisher: DPIIT / IP India

documents.reason: Verified as the original 2001 Rules and therefore superseded: IP India separately publishes Designs (Amendment) Rules of 2008, 2014 and 2021, and a consolidated e-version incorporating amendments through 25 January 2021. The local copy predates all three.

recommended_source.title: The Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Rules, 2002
recommended_source.publisher: DPIIT / IP India

documents.reason: Verified but superseded: the IP India GI rules page also publishes Amendment Rules of 2020 and 2025, neither of which is in the local copy. The base 2002 text is sound; the amendments must be acquired.

recommended_source.title: The Patents Rules, 2003
recommended_source.publisher: Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (IP India), DPIIT — republished through India Code

documents.reason: STALE by nine years. The IP India landing page states its e-version is 'updated till 15-03-2024'; the resolved PDF behind that page could not be captured, so the replacement is identified but not yet acquired. Reports of a Patents (Amendment) Rules, 2025 rest only on secondary sources and are recorded as unconfirmed.

recommended_source.title: Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (Annex 1C to the Marrakesh Agreement Establishing the World Trade Organization)
recommended_source.publisher: World Trade Organization

documents.reason: SUBSTANTIVELY OUT OF DATE, and this is the finding that shows why 'treaties do not go stale' is the wrong rule. The local copy states on its own face that it is the 1994 unamended text. It therefore lacks Article 31bis and the Annex and Appendix inserted by the 2005 Protocol, which entered into force on 23 January 2017 — the compulsory-licensing-for-export provisions most relevant to public health and pharmaceutical patents. The WTO now serves the amended text as the default. Whether India has accepted the Protocol was not confirmed from a WTO source in this phase and must be established before the amended text is treated as binding on India.

recommended_source.publisher: National Biodiversity Authority, Chennai

documents.reason: Current instrument; replaces the 2014 ABS Guidelines. Only the publisher's own hosted copy is missing, not the document's identity.

recommended_source.title: The Biological Diversity Rules, 2024
recommended_source.publisher: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change — republished through India Code

documents.reason: The notification date could not be confirmed from a publisher of record and is left null: secondary sources give 22, 25 and 28 October 2024 inconsistently, and MoEFCC deep links return 404. The G.S.R. number here is taken from the local document itself, not from secondary reporting. These Rules supersede the Biological Diversity Rules, 2004.

recommended_source.title: The Copyright Rules, 2013
recommended_source.publisher: Copyright Office, DPIIT

documents.reason: The local copy is the file the Copyright Office serves today. A Copyright (Amendment) Rules, 2021 exists and is published separately by IP India; it is not incorporated here and should be acquired as a supplementary instrument. Its G.S.R. number is disputed between 225(E) and 226(E) across secondary sources and is recorded as unresolved — no primary gazette copy was obtained.

recommended_source.title: The Designs Act, 2000 (Act No. 16 of 2000)
recommended_source.publisher: India Code, Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice

documents.reason: Absent from the Jan Vishwas 2026 Schedule. The local PDF carries the India Code per-page stamp on every page, which identifies the publisher beyond doubt. It could not be matched against a fetched copy because indiacode.nic.in refuses automated retrieval (handle pages 404, bitstream PDFs 302 to an error page) and indiacode.gov.in serves a JavaScript shell with no content. Verified by direct probe on 2026-08-30, not merely reported.

recommended_source.title: FSSAI Order dated 25 July 2025 — Ayurveda Aahara covered under the Food Safety and Standards (Ayurveda Aahara) Regulations, 2022, with enclosures
recommended_source.publisher: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, Science and Standards Division, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

documents.reason: VERIFIED AS WHAT IT IS, NOT AS WHAT IT WAS FILED UNDER. This file is the FSSAI Order of 25 July 2025 plus a 170-page scanned index of Ayurveda Aahara preparations and their textual references. It is not the Regulations. Its filename in the corpus asserts otherwise and must not be trusted; the Regulations are registered separately as IN-FSSAI-AYURVEDA-AAHARA-REGS-2022, status MISSING. Confirmed again in this phase: the FSSAI 'Ayurveda Aahara Compendium' (647 pages, fetched from fssai.gov.in) is likewise a recipe index containing no regulatory prose.
